title: Fred Maywald confirms the story in recorded call
summary: Robert Salas tells of Fred Maywald confirms the story in recorded call, about 1967; recorded later at Oscar Flight, Montana, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.link_reason: Both are Salas's later contact with his commander Fred Maywald, which confirmed the account. Here that contact is dated 1996, and it is when Salas learned he was at Oscar Flight.

as_told.title: Salas learns in 1996 he was at Oscar, not Echo Flight

plain: Robert Salas, a former US Air Force officer, says that in 1967, while he was on duty at a nuclear missile site in Montana called Oscar Flight, a UFO appeared and ten nuclear missiles shut down. Salas says that in 1996 he finally reached his old commander, Fred Maywald, who confirmed the essentials of the story on a recorded call now posted on the website spiralgalaxy.org, and that the call showed Salas had been at Oscar Flight, not a nearby site called Echo Flight. If true, it would mean something unknown could switch off America's nuclear weapons.
